ev.q: From 2020 to 2021, the age-adjusted death rate (AADR) increased by 0.7%, from 835.4 to 841.6 per 100,000 standard population.
COVID-19 was the underlying cause for 13.3% of all deaths in 2021, increasing from 10.4% (350,831 deaths) in 2020.
COVID-19 was reported as the underlying cause or a contributing cause in an estimated 460,513 (13.3%) of those deaths (111.4 deaths per 100,000).
COVID-19 was the underlying cause for 13.3% of all deaths in 2021, increasing from 10.4% (350,831 deaths) in 2020.
Overall and COVID-19 death rates decreased for Hispanic, Black, and Asian persons from 2020 to 2021.
AADRs were calculated for deaths by sex and race and ethnicity.
This report presents an overview of provisional U.S. mortality data for 2021, including a comparison of death rates for 2020 and 2021.
Provisional death counts and rates for 2021 were compared with final 2020 data
